title: Decay and pole strength
subtitle: Material, location and the remaining shell

chapters.title: Begin with sound timber
chapters.text: An intact surface can conceal deterioration.  Here the cut face contains sound timber. In bending, fibres farther from the centre have greater leverage. The location of damage therefore matters, as well as its size.

chapters.title: Decay is not always a cavity
chapters.text: Decay weakens wood without leaving a hole.  This section has central decay, becoming less severe away from its source.  The distribution is prescribed: an illustrative material penalty, not a forecast of decay growth.

title: Before anyone climbs
subtitle: Condition, demands and an approved decision rule

chapters.text: A pole can look sound while hiding deterioration.  Appearance is only part of inspection. These outside and cut-face images are model views, not field evidence. A pre-climb assessment must consider more.

title: Introducing Safe2Climb
subtitle: A structured inspection and an auditable record

chapters.title: Structure the inspection
chapters.text: A pre-climb inspection needs a clear sequence and a record of what happened.  Safe2Climb guides the inspector through the pole, attachments, setting, movement and base condition. Each step keeps observations connected to the inspection, making the process easier to review.

Each step keeps observations connected to the inspection, making the process easier to review.
